newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - FX vols flat but dealers wary of surprise.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - FX vols flat but dealers wary of surprise.

text.p: Implied volatilities for short-dated dollar/pair options were near unchanged in early afternoon trade on Wednesday, but some players remained wary of the potential for an extreme move in a thin holiday market.

"It's the week before Christmas and nobody wants to play," said one over-the-counter (OTC) dealer with a Canadian bank. "All I can say is it will probably be four days of this and one day of extreme excitement before the end of the year."
In thin holiday trade, a large player could cause such excitement, as could a dramatic fall in the U.S. stock market, he said.
"If we had some kind of cataclysmic 150 point downturn (in the Dow) the dollar would take a dive on that and that might get the market moving. But it's going to take something like that," he said.
Although trade was very light, concern that such an event could occur was preventing volatilities from sliding as much as might have been expected, dealers said.
At 1215 CST/1815 GMT, implied volatility for one-month dollar/mark options was up 0.20 percentage point from Tuesday's U.S. close at 8.6 percent, dealers said.
Implied volatility for one-month dollar/yen was down 0.10 percentage point at 7.9/8.0 percent.
Continued strength in the British pound was holding cable volatility firm and providing a few strains of interest in an otherwise monotone market, dealers said.

Following Tuesday's sterling rally during the U.S. session, traders in London and Asia became nervous. As a result, implied volatility opened Wednesday's U.S. session at 9.0/9.4 percent, compared with 9.0/9.1 percent at close Tuesday. However, by noon, volatility had drifted back down to the latter level, another OTC dealer said.
"Some of the buying in six-months and nine-months (cable) has been off the back of exotics activity," he added, referring to tailor-made barrier options.
However, the other dealers had not heard of this activity.
"You may not see a lot between now and the holidays," a dealer with a Japanese bank added.
"Basically people have extremely flat positions so there isn't a whole lot to hurt them," the first dealer said.
"And let's face it, if you haven't made your budget now, you're not going to make it in the next five days." ((D Bochove, 312 408-8750 E-mail: derivatives@reuters.com))
